precepts.text: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Go ahead and try to do it another way; a lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord.
precepts.point: On the 501c3 accusation: a 501c3 is just a tax classification, meaning we do not pay tax; when we spend at the store we keep the tax money and buy more unleavened bread. It is not a check that gets cut. And if you think we had to stop teaching the commandments and faith in Christ for it, look what we are teaching; nobody cut the feed and nobody cut the funding.

note.label: Member's In The Body

precepts.why:
Build any other way and it is going to fall. “Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.”

Go ahead and try to do it another way. A lot of these organizations are finding out what happens when you build on anything other than the Lord. Some built their whole congregation on fear. They ran to Egypt because they thought the judgment was coming in 2012. Brothers got their passports, not to go teach but to try to deliver themselves; they left Babylon and literally led their people into a civil war, talking about safety and security. We are not built like that; this foundation is built on the rock.

Black people have the attitude that we can't build anything for ourselves and that the other nations, especially the white man, have to get involved for us to succeed. We have a totally different mindset. The Bishop always taught: make sure we have our own and never depend on anybody, because the enemy can shut you down any minute. Nobody is backing us up, and we don't need anybody to. We need each other. Together we can move mountains.

That is why we have had the success we've had: the Lord built the house. And this is just the beginning; you have not seen anything yet.

precepts.text: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it; the house is the house of marriage and, by extension, Israel. If the world builds it you get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people. It is vain to eat the bread of sorrows, woe is me in my marriage, when God is on your side to fix it. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord; as arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are children of the youth; happy is the man that hath his quiver full, they shall speak with the enemies in the gate. They fill your shoes to point out the evils of our oppressors and our people and offer the hope of salvation.
precepts.point: Genesis 1:28, be fruitful and multiply: marriage is nation building, which implies children if you are able. Joshua 24:15: choose you this day whom ye will serve, but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. He builds his house so the children have integrity also.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.” Why are they blessed? Because he raised a stable, sound household. The other purpose of marriage is “Be fruitful, and multiply”: marriage is nation building, and that implies children if you are able. Psalms 127 explains why.

“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the Lord keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.” The house is the house of marriage, the foundation of it, and by extension Israel as a people. That is why it is so important to handle this right: if you let the world build the house, you are going to get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people.

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Why put yourself in a situation and then say woe is me, I am miserable in my marriage, full of sorrows, as if you had no control, power or authority, and as if God were not on your side to fix it?

He did not randomly decide to talk about children; he started with building a house. “Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” That is how we carry on. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.” If the just man walks in his integrity, his children are in good condition.

“Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed.” They are not ashamed because you raised them godly, and it is not only what you tell them but what they see and experience in you as an example. “but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate”: that is the purpose. They follow behind you and fill your shoes, to point out the evils of our oppressors, to point out the evils of our people, and to give them the hope of salvation that they know not.

So the children of the just man are blessed after him because of Psalms 127: the Lord built the house, and the man kept his integrity in it.

precepts.text: Children are the heritage and gift of the Lord, one of the things we understand come of Him.
precepts.point: Whoso is wise and will observe these things, even they shall understand the lovingkindness of the Lord. If you have wisdom you will observe these things.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

This is one of the things we understand come of him. Whoso is wise and will observe these things understands the lovingkindness of the Lord.

precepts.text: We are no more strangers and foreigners, no more so-called blacks and Spanish and native Indians, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God.
precepts.point: When the spirit of the Most High comes upon you and you come into this truth, the many different skill sets we have come together to build up the house of the Lord, just like in the days of old. We are one body through the spirit.

precepts.why:
“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it”. The house being referred to is us. We represent God’s house, and we have to be built up in these scriptures.

“Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God”. No more so-called blacks and Spanish and native Indians, but fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God, the house the Most High is building.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
The house is “built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. We labor in vain if we do not build it upon this Bible.

We have had many groups in the past, the Black Panthers and many other groups of our people, and the only reason they did not succeed is because they did not build the house upon the prophets and the apostles in Christ. We have to be built on the foundation of this Bible: our forefathers the prophets, the apostles, and Christ as our leader, the King of kings and Lord of lords, Jesus Christ.

precepts.text: Israel is the beloved; the Most High hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.
precepts.point: For so he giveth his beloved sleep. He gives the Israelites rest, rest from the bread of sorrows.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
“for so he giveth his beloved sleep.” Israel is the beloved: the Most High hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. “Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.”

He gives the Israelites rest, rest from the bread of sorrows. It is vain to rise up early and sit up late to eat the bread of sorrows, vain to labor and build without the apostles, the prophets, and Christ as our leader; the rest is given to his beloved.

precepts.text: Thou hast discontinued from thine heritage that I gave thee; we have been disconnected from our heritage.
precepts.point: These are the curses we are under. Our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings and from our homeland.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
“Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord”. The children are our inheritance. But “thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

We have been disconnected and discontinued from our heritage, including our children. These are the curses we are under, serving our enemies in a land we knew not.

Children are an heritage of the Lord, and the law of life is the heritage that restores a people disconnected from theirs.

precepts.text: For Isaac's sake he made the blessing rest upon the head of Jacob, gave him an heritage, and divided his portions among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: These are the curses we are under. Our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings and from our homeland.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
For Isaac’s sake, for Abraham his father’s sake, the Most High established the blessing and the covenant, and “made it rest upon the head of Jacob.” He acknowledged him in his blessing, “and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.”

That heritage divided among the twelve tribes is what we have been disconnected and discontinued from. Children are an heritage of the Lord, part of the portion given to Jacob, and we are still under the curses that cut us off from it.

precepts.text: Isaac says, behold now I am old, I know not the day of my death.
precepts.point: Why in their youth? Because they are in a heritage to carry on your name and to meet the enemy in the gate. It is very important to raise our children in God's laws so they understand who the enemy is.

precepts.why: “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth.” Isaac says, “Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death”. A man does not know the day of his death, and that is why children of the youth matter: they are a heritage to carry on your name after you are gone.
